title: Anna's Reel
author: Rick Mohr
notes: The Caller's Box 140, permission: full. **A two-pass record** (M8): the phrase list holds both passes in order, `A1 A2 B1 B2 2A1 2A2 2B1 2B2`, and `passes: 2` says so. The set progresses at the end of **each** pass, and the second pass exchanges the roles throughout — which is why it is written out rather than derived, and which is the consequence of the progression below rather than a coincidence. A1's wave of four runs **across** the set (`balance-wave-of-four`). **The swap-sides progression is a record field** (M8b): `"progression": { "places": { "lark": 1, "robin": 1 }, "line": "swap" }` — one dancing place along and everybody crosses to the other line, keeping the way they were travelling, which is the Caller's Box's own "other; single, swap sides" and puts the other role on each line, so the second pass is the first danced by the other role. Measured, it is the right mechanism: **closure went from 20.0000/37.7359 px at every length to 0.0000 at 2, 4 and 6 couples**, and reach from 25.5193 px short to 0.2194. `37.7359` was always `sqrt(32^2 + 20^2)`, across the set *and* one place along, and the 32 is the swap. **The half hey ends short, and the `~` says so** (M9c). Written without it, four tokens are *five* legs (`legsOfPassList` counts the walk home), so the declared `amount: 0.5` was silently overridden to 0.625 - five eighths of the weave, a shift of 225 degrees. The hey's four phases are quarter turns, so an odd multiple of 45 degrees puts every dancer's target exactly on the bisector between two places, every gap in `planSchedule`'s landing search ties at 45.0000 degrees, and the tie went to list order: two dancers on one floor point (`c1/lark` and `c1/robin` both on (24, 30) at four couples, `collision 0.000 px` at every length, at beat 32). `~` is what the record meant all along - "you get there and stop", and the fourth meeting *is* where the dance stops, because B1 is the robins' balance and swing. With it the legs are four, the amount is the 0.5 the record already declared, the ends go through `settleOnPlaces`, which cannot put two dancers on one place, and **`progressed` falls from 37.7359 px to 32.0000 at 4, 5 and 6 couples** - the swap alone, with the spurious extra couple place gone. **Still owed, one thing, measured: `collision`.** At 4, 5 and 6 couples it is **2.143 px** at **beat 8.625**, `c2/robin ~ c3/robin` inside A1's `balance-wave-of-four` - a figure-internal spacing that has been there at every length since the dance was encoded and is not the end effect or the hey. At 2 and 3 couples it is still 0.000 px, at the cycle seam: at two couples the swap leaves *both* couples standing out and their two wait groups on one pair of points (beat 66); at three, `c1/lark ~ c2/robin` at beat 128, a `walk-to-station` standing where an `allemande` starts. A line of two or three is short for a dance whose progression swaps the whole set. (2) closure still fails at the **odd** lengths — 37.7359 px at 3 couples and 32.0000 at 5 — where a duple improper line has a waiting couple and the swap has a second end effect the lattice shift does not reproduce. **M9f: the two robins were passing through each other on the way out of their own swing.** `orbitPair`'s `settle` read "the lark opens out on the left of the way the pair faces, the robin on its right" off the *dancers'* roles, and B1's `balance-and-swing` is `pairs: [["1R","2R"]]` - two robins, both answering `robin`, so the test fell through to "the first of the pair", a coin toss with nothing to do with where the two of them stand. When it lost, the two end places were named the wrong way round, and a swing's bodies are lerped from the orbit straight to their ends, so both were dragged across the centre at once: measured `collision 3.6187 px` at **beat 47** (and 175, 2B1's two larks) at every checked length. The ends now go **by position** - the end of the orbit each dancer finishes on, which `round: "open"` fixes at `facing + 90` - and only for a pair whose two dancers share a role, so every mixed pair in the corpus is bit-for-bit what it was and the fifteen programme dances' oracle rows are identical at every length. Measured, before -> after: **collision 0.0000 / 3.6187 / 3.4803 px -> 5.9634 (2 couples), 4.4980 (3), 4.0915 (4, 5, 6)**; `progressed` 20.0000/32.0000 -> a uniform 37.7359 px, because the two robins now finish on the other two of the four places. `set/sameRoleEnds.test.ts` is the fixture, ten cases, all ten failing without the fix. **Still owed, and it is now two things, both measured.** (1) `collision 4.0915 px` at **beat 136.5**, `c0/lark ~ c3/lark`: the **two minor sets' `balance-wave-of-four` rows crossing at the boundary between them**, both dancers at y = 30 with the two rows centred at y = 10 and y = 50. On a `line: "swap"` pass the lattice's lines and the floor's are the other way round, so all four of a row cross the whole set to reach it (`c0/robin` walks `(-16, 20) -> (21, 31)` in the one beat the row closes over) and FR-A2's bow is what keeps the pass off zero. Laying the row out the way that walks least was **measured and not taken**: 4.0915 -> 4.7959 px at 3 and 4 couples, and 4.0915 -> **1.9482** at 5 and 6, where two neighbouring minor sets' heys then reach into each other at beat 93.125. It is the wave's orientation, it is free, and it wants a look ruling rather than a tie-break. (2) The dance also fails **motion**, on `main` and after: `balance-wave-of-four` at elbow **225.0** px/beat (bound 188.3), elbow/hand **49.19x** (bound 9.89) and travel **26.3** px/beat (bound 23.32), and `allemande` at elbow/hand **21.10x** and travel **25.4**. Neither row is in `motionAllowlist.ts`, so `pnpm dance annas-reel` is FAIL on motion whatever the collision does, and the dance cannot be promoted until those are owned. **M9g: the wave's motion is the figure's path, not the gait.** Measured at four couples over beats 8 to 9, which is `balance-wave-of-four`'s own first beat: the row is laid out across the set at `x = -21, -7, 7, 21` and the four dancers are on the formation's places at `x = +-16`, so **two of them cross most of the set to reach it in one beat** - `c0/robin` walks `(16, 20) -> (-7, 9)`, 27.3 px, and `c1/robin` `(-16, 0) -> (7, 11)`, 25.5 px - while the other two step 10.3 px. That one beat *is* the `travel 26.3` row, and the `elbowPerHand 49.19x` with it: the wave's hands are joined over a floor point that is already fixed while two bodies are still travelling to it, so the hand hardly moves and the elbow swings the whole way. **So it is the figure's path (FR-A2's), and M10's gait cannot reach it**: no profile makes a 27 px beat into a 23 px one. What the card says is *"Women allemande right 1 & 1/2"* into *"Balance wave of four"* - the allemande is supposed to **leave** the robins in the wave, and today it settles them back on the formation's places and the balance has to build the row from scratch. Writing that as the call's own clause - `"form": { "shape": "wave" }` on the allemande, which is the mechanism `interpret.ts`'s `targetOf` documents in those very words - was **measured and changed nothing**: every oracle row and every motion row identical in every digit, because the allemande's instance casts only the two robins and a wave of four is a shape of all four. The lever is the wave's own formation over its first beat, or an allemande that can form a four-dancer shape from a two-dancer instance. `progressed` is 37.7359 px = sqrt(32^2 + 20^2) at every length, the swap-sides progression carried by nothing, and it is the second thing owed.
